brief: US equities fell Thursday (S&P 500 -2%, Nasdaq -2.3%) on AI-trade concerns plus a more hawkish rate backdrop, and the selloff spread to Asia Friday (Nikkei over -5%, Taiwan -6.2%). Fed October minutes showed nearly all policymakers expecting further tightening if the economy evolves as anticipated, with markets pricing a near-certain 25bp December hike. The dollar held gains and gold slid to a 14-month low near $3,575/oz, down 1.3% Friday and 8% on the week. AMD fell 7.7% on a short-sell report tied to China chip-restriction fears, and NVIDIA fell 3.3% despite an upbeat forecast. UBS says the AI investment and earnings story has not broken, but it cut global equities to Neutral from Attractive on elevated expectations, concentration (top 10 companies are 39% of the S&P 500), and AI-outcome uncertainty, as the debate shifts from whether AI investment continues to whether it earns adequate returns (cumulative capex near $5tr by 2028 needs roughly $1.5tr of AI revenue by 2030). It prefers Eurozone equities, industrials, health care, intermediate-duration bonds and EM/high-yield debt, and targets gold near $5,000/oz in late 2027. Alibaba's cloud revenue grew 53% y/y, and Tencent's cloud growth accelerated to 35% y/y but with negative free cash flow.
